Senses.PreferredTarget: the last word or final phrase
Senses.Explanation: The last word or final phrase: in Zen records, a stock public question about the decisive final saying, and in death or memorial records, an actual final utterance. Its central case is the Deshan–Yantou story. Xuefeng reports Deshan's conduct to Yantou, who says that Deshan has not yet grasped the last word (老漢未會末後句在). Asked for it, Yantou answers only, “want to know the last word? Just this” (要識末後句，只者是). The phrase becomes the stock question “what is the last word?” (如何是末後句), receiving many recorded answers. Other texts set it beside the first word and middle word, or place it at the last locked barrier. In death and memorial settings, Zhongfeng Mingben criticizes calling seated or standing death “the last word,” Tianning Xipu uses the phrase in his death scene, Foyan Qingyuan invokes his deceased teacher's final phrase, and Sixin Wuxin answers a last-word request with a verse before dying. The sample therefore preserves both deployments of one expression instead of silently making every occurrence chronological or every occurrence technical.
Senses.Note: The phrase occurs more than one thousand times across more than two hundred allowlisted texts. The Deshan–Yantou case recurs across independent records, while the bare challenge and death or memorial uses have their own spread. The former “last word” and “final words at death” targets described a general phrase and a contextual subtype of that same phrase; they remain together because several death-scene examples deliberately use the stock Zen phrase rather than a merely chronological label. Compare the way up and beyond, upward dynamic, last locked barrier, turning phrase, late teacher's last word, memorial morning, and dying seated or standing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪峰舉似巖頭。頭曰：「老漢未會末後句在。」山謂頭曰：「你不肯老僧那？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Abridged Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guting (古庭禪師語錄輯略) reproduces Yantou Quanhuo's verdict that Deshan Xuanjian has not yet grasped the last word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧到巖頭舉似頭。頭云：「雪峰不會末後句。」僧請益巖頭。頭云：「雪峰與我同條生，不與我同條死。要識末後句，只者是。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Abridged Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guting (古庭禪師語錄輯略) reproduces Yantou Quanhuo's answer: 'Want to know the last word? Just this.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 小德山未會末後句在。山聞。令侍者喚師去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): complete-case exact-turn review identifies Yantou Quanhuo as the actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是末後句。師曰。雙林樹下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): inside Xuansha Shibei's section, an unnamed monk asks what the final phrase is; Xuansha answers 'beneath the paired sala trees.' The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not give a personal name for the unnamed questioning monk.
The Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄): Zhongfeng Mingben criticizes people who call seated or standing death the 'final phrase' in his own extended address.
